steps.text: Sift flour, sugar, and salt into a bowl; set aside. Beat eggs and milk together in a large bowl with an electric mixer.
Beat in flour mixture until smooth; stir in melted butter.
Lightly grease a griddle or frying pan; heat over medium-high heat. Pour or scoop the batter onto the griddle, using approximately 2 tablespoons for each crêpe.
Immediately rotate the skillet to spread batter out in a thin layer. Cook until the top of the crêpe is no longer wet and the bottom has turned light brown, 1 to 2 minutes.
Shake the pan or loosen with a spatula; turn or flip it over and cook until other side has turned light brown, about 1 minute more. Repeat with remaining batter.
Serve with your choice of fillings or toppings, and enjoy!

raw_recipe.headline: French Crêpes
raw_recipe.description: These French crêpes are thin, delicate, and delicious for breakfast or dessert. Fill as you like with fresh berries, jam, or chocolate spread.

review.reviewBody: This is an excellent recipe! Some suggestions for people who say the batter is thin and the edges are crispy. First, when you make crepes, you have to tilt the hot, slightly greasy pan and pour the batter in the from the edges. DO NOT start in the center or else you will end up with "the batter would settle to the center before setting" as stated in an earlier comment. Secondly, immediately after you cook them, place them in a tupperware with the lid covering them, but NOT sealed. This will keep them warm and moisten the edges and other crispy areas. This is the perfect crepe recipe! The taste and consistency are on point. So any complaints people have about this recipe is not because of the batter, it's because of not cooking them correctly. These are great and truly easy to make!

Outstanding. Followed some tips of another user. I used a medium sized pan on med high heat, sprayed with pam before each crepe. Used a ladle about 3/4 full poured all in on one side and then rotated the pan to cover. Once it started bubbling worked the spatula in and flipped.
Phenomenonal taste. I served with Nutella and strawberries inside. Topped with powdered sugar and maple syrup (real syrup only).

This recipe is excellent - and versatile. Great as-is for a sweet filling (I like a little more sugar - personal preference) (or to eat plain - SO good) To make it savory, I leave out the sugar, add parsley or other herbs then fill with ricotta cheese, prosciutto, bacon, ham, etc. VERY easy but as others mentioned, if you are having trouble it's most likely with the pan and the temp. I use a setting just below Medium on my gas range, a small pan which I mop with olive oil every 3-4 crepes and just keep rolling the pan until the batter sets - flip it when it loosens from the pan and cook the other side for just a few second - 'voila! Excellent! (and everyone will think you're an accomplished french chef!

this is by far the easiest crepe recipe I've come across. I don't have a stand or hand mixer so I just throw everything in a blender, the batter came out perfect. when you pour in the batter, make sure is away from the heat, tilt the pan and try to make the batter distribute equally throughout the pan. It takes practice to be perfect. Also another key is your pan retains heat, and every stove is different. I found that for medium-high heat for my stove and pan combo was way too hot. I ended up started at medium heat, after maybe 4 crepes I had to turn the heat down to medium-low.
All around 5 stars recipe I'll be making it as a breakfast meal prep for the week. Happy cooking!

Delicious! If you’re using large eggs with deep yolks I recommend only using 2. I used 3 large eggs the first time I made this and the crêpes had a bit of an omelette aroma and were leaning yellow; so I made this again with 2 large eggs instead of 3 and that solved that.

My Great Grandmother came over from Germany with an amazing Crepe recipe and I could not find it anywhere. I am so happy I found this, it is exactly like her recipe!! 

I found that the correct size pan and the right temperature is the key to a perfect crepe. I keep the setting a little higher than is needed, but I am constantly picking up the pan. I pick up the pan and pour a ladle full of mix into it as I am tipping it around and then put on the stovetop. When it becomes loose in the pan, I pick up the pan off the stove top and flip it over. It doesn't need long at all to cook the other side and then I pick it up again and slide it onto a plate and then start the entire process over again. 
 
Our favorite filling is Nutella and cut up ripe bananas with a couple of bananas on top with Nutella drizzled over. Heavenly for sure!

I make ahead of time and freeze with parchment paper between each crepe and reheat and stuff when all the family is over. Quick and easy. 

So happy I found this recipe, I will make it again and again with zero modifications.

I’ve been making this recipe from All Recipes for years and it’s great. This morning I tried it by mixing everything in my smoothie blender (i have a nutri bullet). Eggs, milk, then flour and salt, then olive oil. They came out better than ever, and soooooo easy. 

Because we don’t do dairy, I use unsweetened almond milk and olive oil in place of butter and milk. Works fine. I don’t add sugar anymore because I usually pair my crepes with a mix of sweet and savory. The sugar way is fine too. 

This recipe has been the right mix of flour, egg and milk for me always. I am French and learned how to make crepes in France, but this is an easier recipe but still gives me the result I want. 
I like that you don’t have to wait on the batter either (I was taught to let it sit for an hour). I also store the batter and cook crepes up later with this recipe. 

I use a few drops on olive oil on my nonstick pan and swirl them around with a paper towel and that way have no issues with stickiness.
I did a well in the center of the bowl instead of using 2 bowls and I do 3/4 teaspoon sugar and not 1 taespoon

I've made this recipe about 15 times now and I even though my first few attempts weren't perfect, I have found it to be a perfect crepe recipe. To get it perfect I make a few changes to the process.
First I mix the eggs alone, then add the milk. I make sure the milk is room temperature, it always makes it better! 
Then I add in the rest of the ingredients. 
Once mixed, the batter gets better the longer it sits so if you have time try and leave it for at least 10/15mins.
The biggest problem with this recipe is that my family eat them all so quickly there's hardly any left for me!! 
Thanks for a fantastic recipe!

Best recipe for crepes. Here are some tips I have acquired through many trials. Let your batter sit for at least 1/2 hour . I use a blender and leave it in the container, when ready I give a few quick pulses, my pan sits with no butter on slightly above medium until hot and use a paper towel with the smallest amount of butter and wipe to coat I then have a 1/4 cup of batter ready set your pan back on burner for a few seconds and pour the measured batter and use your wrist to coat quickly. Adjust the burner as you go. Be patient the first one or two usually don't look the greatest but still taste light, beautifully thin, I have tried at least 5 different recipes and this one is my go to favorite. Thanks cyberchef

This was, by far, the best crepe recipe I've ever used. I did add a little vanilla as I was making a breakfast/dessertish crepe:) For the size of my crepe pan, two tablespoons was not quite sufficient. I used 1/4 cup (4 tablespoons) and felt that they came out just right and for those of you who felt they were too crispy, it may be that you just need to add slightly more batter to the pan. The crepes were flavorful and easy to work with when putting in the filling. This will be my go to recipe for crepes in the future.
Makes a solid crepe! Easy recipe to adjust if needed
Pretty good, I did add a bit of vanilla.
Yummy. I don't recommend cooking on med/high. Medium heat is sufficient.
you need ice creem! it make's it better
Super simple and a real staple
Bit more sugar and salt required. I also add lemon zest. Then fill with a bit of sugar and a squeeze of lemon juice.
